Buckling-Constrained Truss Optimization with SDP Constraints

Description

This tutorial demonstrates buckling-constrained topology optimization on a truss structure. The goal is to minimize compliance while ensuring the combined stiffness matrix K + c·Kσ remains positive semidefinite — i.e., the structure does not buckle under the applied load scaled by buckling factor c.

We use differentiable building blocks (ElementK, AssembleK, TrussElementKσ, apply_boundary_with_zerodiag!, apply_boundary_with_meandiag!) and enforce the PSD constraint via semidefinite programming (SDP) using NonconvexSemidefinite.jl with an IPM barrier method.

Setup

using TopOpt, LinearAlgebra, Zygote
using Nonconvex, NonconvexSemidefinite, NonconvexIpopt

Load Truss Geometry

Download the truss geometry file: tim_2d.json.

ndim = 2
node_points, elements, mats, crosssecs, fixities, load_cases = load_truss_json(
    joinpath(@__DIR__, "tim_$(ndim)d.json")
)
ndim, nnodes, ncells = length(node_points[1]), length(node_points), length(elements)
loads = load_cases["0"]
problem = TrussProblem(
    Val{:Linear}, node_points, elements, loads, fixities, mats, crosssecs
)

Parameter Settings

xmin = 0.0001   # minimum density
p = 1.0         # SIMP penalty exponent
V = 0.5         # volume fraction
x0 = fill(1.0, ncells)  # initial design (all solid)

FEA Solver and Buckling Helpers

solver = FEASolver(DirectSolver, problem; xmin=xmin)
ch = problem.ch

comp = TopOpt.Compliance(solver)
dp = TopOpt.Displacement(solver)
assemble_k = TopOpt.AssembleK(problem)
element_k = ElementK(solver)
truss_element_kσ = TrussElementKσ(problem, solver)

Five differentiable building blocks: 1. Compliance — objective to minimize 2. Displacement — solves K·u = f for displacements 3. ElementK — per-element stiffness matrices 4. AssembleK — assembles global sparse matrix 5. TrussElementKσ — geometric (stress) stiffness matrices

Buckling Constraint Function

c = 0.0001  # buckling load multiplier (below critical load)

function buckling_matrix_constr(x)
    xd = PseudoDensities(x)
    u = dp(xd)
    Kes = element_k(xd)
    K = assemble_k(Kes)
    K = apply_boundary_with_meandiag!(K, ch)
    Kσs = truss_element_kσ(u, xd)
    Kσ = assemble_k(Kσs)
    Kσ = apply_boundary_with_zerodiag!(Kσ, ch)
    return Array(K + c * Kσ)
end

The constraint returns the combined matrix K + c·Kσ which must be PSD (all eigenvalues ≥ 0).

Check Initial Design

S0 = buckling_matrix_constr(x0)
println("Initial design minimum eigenvalue: $(minimum(eigen(S0).values))")
Initial design minimum eigenvalue: 0.00045596061885728594

The initial all-solid design should have positive eigenvalues (stable).

Volume Constraint

vol_constr(x) = sum(x) / length(x) - V

Compliance-Only Optimization (Baseline)

obj = x -> comp(PseudoDensities(x))

model = Model(obj)
addvar!(model, zeros(length(x0)), ones(length(x0)))
add_ineq_constraint!(model, vol_constr)

alg = MMA87()
options = MMAOptions(; maxiter=20, tol=Tolerance(; kkt=1e-4))
r1 = optimize(model, alg, x0; options=options)

println("Compliance-only result:")
println("  obj = $(obj(r1.minimizer))")
println("  vol = $(vol_constr(r1.minimizer))")

This baseline ignores buckling — the result may be unstable.

Add Buckling SDP Constraint

# Add semidefinite constraint: K + c·Kσ ≽ 0
add_sd_constraint!(model, buckling_matrix_constr)

alg2 = SDPBarrierAlg(; sub_alg=IpoptAlg())
options2 = SDPBarrierOptions(; 
    sub_options=IpoptOptions(; max_iter=20),
    keep_all=true
)
r2 = optimize(model, alg2, x0; options=options2)

println("Buckling-constrained result:")
println("  obj = $(obj(r2.minimizer))")
println("  vol = $(vol_constr(r2.minimizer))")

  obj = 4.8702962693900576

The SDPBarrierAlg uses an interior-point method with log-barrier for PSD constraints. IPOPT solves the continuous subproblems.

Check Stability

S1 = buckling_matrix_constr(r1.minimizer)
S2 = buckling_matrix_constr(r2.minimizer)

ev1 = eigen(S1).values
ev2 = eigen(S2).values

println("Compliance-only min eigenvalue: $(minimum(ev1))")
println("Buckling-constrained min eigenvalue: $(minimum(ev2))")
println("Design is stable: $(minimum(ev2) ≥ -1e-6)")
Compliance-only min eigenvalue: -1.0058117186307713e-5
Buckling-constrained min eigenvalue: 3.6669304869106886e-9
Design is stable: true

The buckling-constrained design should have non-negative eigenvalues (stable under load), while the compliance-only design may have negative eigenvalues (unstable).

using Makie, CairoMakie

fig2 = visualize(problem; solver.u, topology=r2.minimizer, default_exagg_scale=0.0)
